verses.1: After observing the assembly, Paul said, “Brothers, in all my thoughts and actions, I have served God with all my heart until this day.”
verses.2: The high priest Ananias ordered that those who came to him be forced to open their mouths.
verses.3: Then Paul said to him, “God will make you suffer punishment. You sit there and judge according to the law, yet you yourself break it.”
verses.4: But those who testified said, “Do the priests of God deceive people?”
verses.5: Pavlos said, “Do not know, brothers, that he is an archbishop. It is written that you should not act badly towards the ruler of your people.”
verses.6: Paul knew that one part of the assembly belonged to the Sadducees, while the other part belonged to the Pharisees. Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I judge matters related to hope and the resurrection of the dead.
verses.7: When he spoke in this manner, the Pharisees and Sadducees became angry. The crowd also dispersed.
verses.8: The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit. The Pharisees, however, agree that both exist.
verses.9: A loud cry was heard. Some of the officials from among the Pharisees stood up and began to argue with each other, saying, “We find nothing wrong with this man.” But if it was a spirit or an angel who spoke to him…
verses.10: Fearing the possible outcome of this situation, the commander ordered that the soldiers should capture Paul from among them, and take him away for interrogation.
verses.11: But on the eve of his departure, the Lord said to him, “Tharsis, just as I testified about me in Jerusalem, so too must you testify about me in Jerusalem.”
verses.12: On this day, the Jews decided to take a stand against them. They refused to eat or drink until they killed Paul.
verses.13: And most of those who organized this conspiracy were forty people in total.
verses.14: They went to the high priests and the elders, and said, “We have decided not to taste anything until we kill Paul.”
verses.15: Now, you have shown to the khalip, along with his council, how to bring him closer to you, so that he may be better understood in the future. We, however, must be prepared to receive him before we can do anything else.
verses.16: And the son of Paul’s sister heard about the fire that had broken out, and he went into the area where it was happening and told Paul about it.
verses.17: Pavlos, having invited one of the one hundred men, said, “Take this young man away from the centurion. He has some secrets that he should not reveal to him.”
verses.18: So, after taking him away, he brought him before the khilarikhon. He said, “The bound Paulos invited me over and asked this young man to come to you. He said that he would tell you something interesting.”
verses.19: The chilarch, having taken his hand, moved away from him. What do you have to tell me?
verses.20: He said that the Jews should unite together and try to bring Paul to the assembly tomorrow, so that they can discuss him more carefully.
verses.21: So you won’t be able to persuade them. In fact, more than forty men from their own ranks will rise up against him. They have refused to eat or drink until he is brought back to life. And now they’re ready to accept the message from you.
verses.22: So, the khilairarch dismissed the young man, telling him not to complain at all, since he had revealed these things to me.
verses.23: And having invited two of the hundred men, he said, “Prepare one hundred soldiers who can be sent to Caesarea. Also, prepare seventy cavalrymen and right-handers, starting from the third hour of the night.”
verses.24: I will also present a plan so that they can rescue Paul from Philemon’s hands.
verses.25: Write an email in this format.
verses.26: May Kláudios Lysias be happy with the reigning king, Phílikos.
verses.27: I know that this man has been captured by the Jews, and he will soon be executed by them. I also know that he is a Roman.
verses.28: He wanted to find out the reason why they called for him; so he brought him before their assembly.
verses.29: He was found to be guilty of violating their laws. However, he did not commit any crimes that would warrant death or imprisonment.
verses.30: I also sent you a message, asking that you not try to influence the man on your own. Also, tell the prosecutors to deal with him in your place.
verses.31: Thus, the soldiers, following the arrangements made for them, brought Paul to Antipatris during the night.
verses.32: At the end, they brought back the soldiers with him to participate in the battle.
verses.33: When they entered Caesarea and brought the letter to the governor, they also presented it to Paul as well.
verses.34: And after asking where it came from, he learned that it originated from Kilikia.
verses.35: I warn you, he said, that even your judges may become corrupt. You ordered that they be kept in the prison of Herodes.
